blocks.text: Cloud and container weaknesses are mostly misconfiguration: public storage, over-privileged identities, exposed management interfaces, reachable metadata services, and containers or clusters with unsafe defaults. This category covers storage buckets, metadata services, IAM misconfiguration indicators, Kubernetes and Docker API exposure, container breakout preconditions and secrets in images and environment. For metadata access through SSRF see `SSRF/`.

items: Publicly listable or writable buckets and blob containers; exposed pre-signed URLs and SAS tokens
Metadata services (169.254.169.254 and equivalents) reachable from application code
Over-permissive IAM roles, wildcard policies and credentials in environment variables or images
Exposed Docker daemon (2375/2376), Kubernetes API (6443/8080), kubelet (10250/10255), etcd (2379) and dashboards
Privileged containers, mounted Docker socket, host namespaces and dangerous capabilities
Serverless and CI roles with trust-policy gaps; cross-account `AssumeRole` misconfiguration
Public container registries and images containing secrets

blocks.text: Test only accounts, clusters and buckets you own or are authorised to assess. Start unauthenticated and read-only: list a bucket, query an exposed API for its version, read the identity of the current credentials (`sts get-caller-identity`, `kubectl auth whoami`). Use `can-i` style checks to enumerate permissions instead of exercising them. Do not read, copy or delete data from storage you do not own. Stop at proof of access and document the least-privilege fix.
See `cloud-container-payloads.txt` for read-only enumeration commands, exposure checks, metadata endpoints and indicators of risky configuration.

sections.label: AWS S3: anonymous and authenticated exposure checks
Azure Blob / Google Cloud Storage anonymous access checks
Bucket name guessing patterns (own organisation naming)
Pre-signed URL and SAS token review (look in application responses and logs)
Cloud metadata endpoints (from a workload you own; see SSRF for filter bypasses)
Kubernetes API, kubelet and etcd exposure
Kubernetes permission checks from inside a pod (read-only)
Kubernetes manifest review (static analysis on your own YAML)

files.content:
# Cloud and Container Payloads
# Read-only enumeration and exposure checks. Use only against accounts and clusters you own or are authorised to test.

# AWS: identity and permission checks
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws iam get-user
aws iam list-attached-user-policies --user-name <user>
aws iam list-roles --max-items 20
aws iam simulate-principal-policy --policy-source-arn <arn> --action-names s3:GetObject
aws configure list
aws s3 ls
aws ec2 describe-regions --query 'Regions[].RegionName'

# AWS S3: anonymous and authenticated exposure checks
aws s3 ls s3://<bucket> --no-sign-request
aws s3 ls s3://<bucket>
aws s3api get-bucket-acl --bucket <bucket> --no-sign-request
aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket <bucket>
aws s3api get-public-access-block --bucket <bucket>
aws s3api get-bucket-website --bucket <bucket>
aws s3api list-object-versions --bucket <bucket> --no-sign-request --max-items 5
curl -s https://<bucket>.s3.amazonaws.com/
curl -s https://s3.amazonaws.com/<bucket>/
curl -sI https://<bucket>.s3.amazonaws.com/<key>
curl -s -X PUT -d 's3-write-check-marker' https://<bucket>.s3.amazonaws.com/write-check-<unique-token>.txt -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n"

# Azure Blob / Google Cloud Storage anonymous access checks
curl -s "https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net/<container>?restype=container&comp=list"
curl -s "https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net/?comp=list"
curl -s "https://storage.googleapis.com/<bucket>/"
curl -s "https://www.googleapis.com/storage/v1/b/<bucket>/o"
curl -s "https://storage.googleapis.com/storage/v1/b/<bucket>/iam"
gsutil ls gs://<bucket>
az storage container list --account-name <account>
az storage blob list --account-name <account> --container-name <container> --auth-mode login

# Bucket name guessing patterns (own organisation naming)
<company>
<company>-prod
<company>-dev
<company>-staging
<company>-backup
<company>-backups
<company>-assets
<company>-static
<company>-logs
<company>-data
<company>-uploads
<company>-public
<company>-internal
<company>-terraform
<company>-tfstate

# Pre-signed URL and SAS token review (look in application responses and logs)
X-Amz-Signature
X-Amz-Expires=604800
X-Amz-Credential=
sv=2020-08-04&ss=bfqt&srt=sco&sp=rwdlacupx&se=
sig=
GoogleAccessId=
Signature=

# Cloud metadata endpoints (from a workload you own; see SSRF for filter bypasses)
http://169.254.169.254/latest/user-data
curl -s -X PUT "http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token" -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 21600"
http://169.254.170.2/v2/credentials/
http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/?recursive=true
curl -s -H "Metadata-Flavor: Google" http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/
curl -s -H "Metadata: true" "http://169.254.169.254/metadata/identity/oauth2/token?api-version=2018-02-01&resource=https://management.azure.com/"
http://100.100.100.200/latest/meta-data/
http://169.254.169.254/openstack/latest/meta_data.json

# Docker daemon exposure
curl -s http://<host>:2375/version
curl -s http://<host>:2375/containers/json
curl -s http://<host>:2375/images/json
curl -s http://<host>:2375/info
curl -sk https://<host>:2376/version
docker -H tcp://<host>:2375 ps
curl -s --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock http://localhost/containers/json
curl -s http://<host>:5000/v2/_catalog
curl -s http://<host>:5000/v2/<repo>/tags/list

# Kubernetes API, kubelet and etcd exposure
curl -sk https://<host>:6443/version
curl -sk https://<host>:6443/api
curl -sk https://<host>:6443/apis
curl -sk https://<host>:6443/api/v1/namespaces
curl -s http://<host>:8080/api/v1/pods
curl -sk https://<host>:10250/pods
curl -sk https://<host>:10250/runningpods/
curl -s http://<host>:10255/pods
curl -s http://<host>:10255/metrics
curl -s http://<host>:2379/version
curl -s http://<host>:2379/v2/keys/?recursive=true
curl -sk https://<host>:6443/openapi/v2
curl -s http://<host>:8001/api/v1/namespaces
curl -s http://<host>:30000/

# Kubernetes permission checks from inside a pod (read-only)
kubectl auth can-i --list
kubectl auth can-i create pods
kubectl auth can-i get secrets
kubectl auth can-i '*' '*'
kubectl auth whoami
cat /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/namespace
ls /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/
env | grep -iE 'KUBERNETES|SERVICE'

# Container breakout preconditions (indicators, not exploitation)
cat /proc/1/status | grep -i cap
capsh --print
ls -la /var/run/docker.sock
mount | grep -E 'docker.sock|/host|hostPath'
cat /proc/self/cgroup
ls /dev | head
cat /proc/self/status | grep -E 'NoNewPrivs|Seccomp'
securityContext: { privileged: true }
securityContext: { allowPrivilegeEscalation: true }
hostPID: true
hostNetwork: true
hostIPC: true
volumes: - hostPath: { path: / }
capabilities: { add: [SYS_ADMIN] }
capabilities: { add: [SYS_PTRACE] }
capabilities: { add: [NET_ADMIN] }

# Kubernetes manifest review (static analysis on your own YAML)
kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq '.items[]|select(.spec.containers[].securityContext.privileged==true)|.metadata.name'
kubectl get clusterrolebindings -o json | jq '.items[]|select(.subjects[]?.name=="system:anonymous")'
kubectl get secrets -A --no-headers | wc -l
kubectl get roles,clusterroles -A -o json | jq '.items[]|select(.rules[]?.verbs[]?=="*")|.metadata.name'

# Secrets in images and environments
docker run --rm <image> env
docker inspect <image> | jq '.[].Config.Env'
docker history --no-trunc <image>
dive <image>
trivy image --scanners secret <image>
trivy config .
trivy fs --scanners vuln,secret,misconfig .

# Infrastructure-as-code misconfiguration indicators (own repositories)
checkov -d .
tfsec .
terrascan scan
"Principal": "*"
"Action": "*"
"Resource": "*"
"Effect": "Allow", "Action": "iam:PassRole", "Resource": "*"
"Effect": "Allow", "Action": "sts:AssumeRole", "Principal": {"AWS": "*"}
acl = "public-read"
acl = "public-read-write"
cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
publicly_accessible = true
encrypted = false

# Serverless and function exposure
curl -s https://<id>.execute-api.<region>.amazonaws.com/
curl -s https://<region>-<project>.cloudfunctions.net/<function>
curl -s https://<app>.azurewebsites.net/
curl -s https://<function>.azurewebsites.net/api/<name>?code=
